messages:
tara: FYI customer corp-acme reported a mass elevation after a SCIM sync — 8 users became org-admins unexpectedly. They say it happened right after the provisioning job at 2026-03-06T08:12Z. Ticket INC-7890 created.
support-bot: Created INC-7890 · Priority: P1 · Assigned: support@redwood
ben: assigning to sec-ops and identity eng. We need SCIM payload, IDP SAML assertion, and exact mapping rules they used. Also want a copy/export of audit logs for the window.
ashwin: (eng-identity) on it. Tara can you paste the payload/customer-provided logs here? quick check: common issue is group->role mapping mismatch.
tara: customer pasted the payload, sharing sanitized example below:
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "j.smith@acme.com",
  "name": {"givenName": "John", "familyName": "Smith"},
  "groups": ["engineering", "admins"],
  "externalId": "acme-1234"
}
```

tara: they also attached the SAML attributes they receive from their IdP — looks like groups claim contains 'admins' and 'org_admins'.
ashwin: that lines up. Our default mapping currently maps any group containing 'admin' -> org-admin (legacy safe-then behavior). Good catch. We should confirm whether customer intentionally sends those groups. Suggest immediate mitigation: change mapping to look for a dedicated group like 'redwood-org-admin' or require explicit scim role attribute.
olga: (eng-platform) I ran a quick query on audit logs for corp-acme around 2026-03-06T08:00-08:30Z. Found provisioning events by service account scim-service@acme at 08:12:03Z setting role=org-admin for 8 users. Log entries show the action and affected user IDs but no secrets/plaintext in logs.
sec-bot: KMS Audit: logs encrypted at rest with key kms-prod-01 (HSM-backed). Access to logs is via auditer role. No indication keys were exported.
sam: (privacy/compliance) Customer requests full log export and confirmation of retention window for audit logs (they're regulated). Confirm retention is 365 days by default for enterprise customers but we can export a zipped audit bundle.
ashwin: repro steps for internal: 1) create test SCIM token, 2) POST /scim/v2/Users with payload containing groups=["admins"], 3) observe role mapping. Example curl:```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/scim/v2/Users" 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SCIM_TOKEN>' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d @payload.json
```
If the IdP is also sending SAML group assertions on login, the group->role sync can be overwritten depending on their sync precedence.
ben: recommendation checklist to send to customer: 1) rotate SCIM token now, 2) temporarily disable automated role mapping, 3) export audit bundle and share with their security contact, 4) confirm IdP group membership for the affected accounts, 5) apply least-privilege role and run a targeted rollback.
tara: I just asked the customer to rotate their token and to confirm whether admins group membership should translate to org-admin. Waiting on reply. I also asked for the SAML assertion sample if they can provide it.
jake-oncall: i'm oncall, i'll take timeline and open an internal incident with severity P1. I'll also request retention proof and run a KMS access audit. ETA EOD for a timeline.
ben: also flagging this for legal if they claim data exposure. Sam, can you prep a short advisory for customer-facing language we can send?
sam: yes, drafting now. Will advise: (a) no evidence of plaintext key leakage, (b) actions to rotate tokens and update mappings, (c) we'll deliver audit export and timeline.
tara: thanks — i'll keep INC-7890 updated. Marking blocked until customer confirms mapping intent. :eyes: 
ben: thanks team. Once we have the SAML sample we can propose a mapping change and a safer default.
